The core of the packing is the n = 172 arrangement of jlevy/squares#935 (T-282, Doğa Özden after Evan Daniel), re-solved, and the L of 27 squares is #938's (Doğa Özden), as the issue states; the issue credits the core arrangement to Daniel and Özden.
claims: n199/n199_witness.yaml states 199 unit squares, centre and basis (cos, sin) as exact rationals, in a square of exact rational side 1461468985328358057514628890087947061618972730200175769881498026931092424681356737007190165664341823168492765447/10^110, which #939 prints rounded up as 14.61468985328358057514628890087947061619 (and the issue's title as 14.6146898532835806, the root README at 12 places as 14.614689853284). The file follows this repository's Witness/v2 witness object but has no softschema block and no claim, has a notes field, and its id W-n199-de-Winter-locally-optimal has capitals, so this repository's witness schema does not admit it. n199/n199_exact.json states the same packing as [center_x, center_y, cos, sin] rows, with the side and the quintic's coefficients.

The issue and README say the side is less than 1e-98 (the README: 1.4e-99) above the real root near 14.6147 of 62x^5 - 4426x^4 + 125017x^3 - 1746146x^2 + 12052670x - 32855154, which they call irreducible and the local optimum of the arrangement: the optimality conditions of the core were solved to 130 digits, all 734 load-bearing or forced contacts close exactly and all other gaps stay open, and the polynomial was identified numerically from 108 digits and reproduces the side to 129 digits. Local optimality has no formal proof, as the issue says. The packing is a 172-square core and an L of 27 axis-aligned squares, a row of 14 and a column of 13 (s(n + 2 floor(s) + 1) <= s(n) + 1); the core is the arrangement of #935 (Evan Daniel, improved by Doğa Özden), re-optimized to its exact local optimum, a core side of 13.61468985328358..., 2.63e-12 below the value listed at 172.

verify_exact.py (Python standard library, fractions.Fraction) checks exact unit edge directions, containment, a separating-axis test on all 481 pairs with centres closer than sqrt(2), and by an exact sign test that the side lies within 1e-98 above a root of the quintic; the issue says a second script with separate code checked the witness file in the same arithmetic, that the two checkers share one author, the separating-axis test and Python's Fraction, and that the certificate was not replayed with this repository's checkers. The issue says the derivation, local optimization, high-precision solution, rational certificate, checks and figure were produced with Claude (Anthropic) under Joost de Winter's direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
